import pytest
from rich.cells import split_text, _split_text
from rich.segment import Segment
from rich.style import Style


def test_split_text_at_zero_with_single_cells():
    """Split at column 0 with single-cell characters should return empty left and full right."""
    left, right = split_text("hello", 0)
    assert left == ""
    assert right == "hello"


def test_split_text_at_zero_with_mixed_widths():
    """Split at column 0 with mixed width characters should return empty left and full right."""
    # Using emoji (wide characters) mixed with ASCII
    text = "a\u4e00b"  # 'a' (1 cell) + CJK char (2 cells) + 'b' (1 cell)
    left, right = _split_text(text, 0)
    assert left == ""
    assert right == text


def test_split_text_in_middle_single_cells():
    """Split in the middle with single-cell characters."""
    left, right = split_text("hello", 2)
    assert left == "he"
    assert right == "llo"


def test_split_text_at_end_single_cells():
    """Split at or past the end with single-cell characters."""
    left, right = split_text("hello", 5)
    assert left == "hello"
    assert right == ""
    
    left, right = split_text("hello", 10)
    assert left == "hello"
    assert right == ""


def test_split_text_mixed_widths_in_middle():
    """Split in middle of text with mixed width characters."""
    text = "a\u4e00b"  # 1 + 2 + 1 = 4 cells total
    left, right = _split_text(text, 2)
    assert len(left) > 0
    assert len(right) > 0


def test_split_text_within_double_width_char():
    """Split inside a double-width character converts it to spaces."""
    text = "a\u4e00b"  # 'a' (1 cell) + CJK (2 cells) + 'b' (1 cell)
    left, right = _split_text(text, 1)
    # Should split at position 1, which is inside the 2-cell character
    assert left == "a "
    assert right == " b"


def test_segment_split_cells_at_zero_single_cell():
    """Segment.split_cells at column 0 with single-cell text."""
    segment = Segment("hello", Style())
    left, right = segment.split_cells(0)
    assert left.text == ""
    assert right.text == "hello"


def test_segment_split_cells_at_zero_mixed_width():
    """Segment.split_cells at column 0 with mixed width characters."""
    text = "a\u4e00b"
    segment = Segment(text, Style())
    left, right = segment.split_cells(0)
    assert left.text == ""
    assert right.text == text

import pytest
from rich.cells import split_text, _split_text


def test_split_at_boundaries():
    """Test splitting at exact grapheme boundaries."""
    text = "hello"
    
    # Split at 0
    left, right = split_text(text, 0)
    assert (left, right) == ("", "hello")
    
    # Split at 1
    left, right = split_text(text, 1)
    assert (left, right) == ("h", "ello")
    
    # Split at length
    left, right = split_text(text, len(text))
    assert (left, right) == ("hello", "")


def test_split_mixed_single_and_double_cells():
    """Test with mix of single and double-cell characters."""
    # 'a' (1) + CJK (2) + 'b' (1) + CJK (2) = 6 cells
    text = "a\u4e00b\u4e01"
    
    # Split at 0
    left, right = _split_text(text, 0)
    assert left == ""
    assert right == text
    
    # Split at 1
    left, right = _split_text(text, 1)
    assert left == "a"
    assert len(right) > 0
    
    # Split at 3 (right in middle of second CJK char)
    left, right = _split_text(text, 3)
    assert " " in left or " " in right

import pytest

def test_segment_split_cells_boundary_cases():
    """Test split_cells with boundary positions."""
    segment = Segment("test", Style())
    
    # At start
    left, right = segment.split_cells(0)
    assert left.text == ""
    assert right.text == "test"
    assert left.cell_length == 0
    assert right.cell_length == 4
    
    # At end
    left, right = segment.split_cells(4)
    assert left.text == "test"
    assert right.text == ""
    assert left.cell_length == 4
    assert right.cell_length == 0
    
    # Past end
    left, right = segment.split_cells(10)
    assert left.text == "test"
    assert right.text == ""


def test_segment_split_cells_with_wide_characters():
    """Test split_cells with wide characters in segment."""
    # Mix of ASCII and wide chars
    segment = Segment("a\u4e00b", Style())
    
    left, right = segment.split_cells(0)
    assert left.text == ""
    assert right.text == "a\u4e00b"

import pytest
from rich.cells import split_text, _split_text, split_graphemes


def test_split_graphemes_structure():
    """Verify split_graphemes returns correct structure."""
    text = "hello"
    spans, total_width = split_graphemes(text)
    
    assert len(spans) == 5
    assert total_width == 5
    
    # Each span should be (start, end, cell_length)
    for start, end, cell_len in spans:
        assert start < end
        assert cell_len >= 0


def test_split_at_zero_empty_left():
    """Core test: split at 0 returns empty left."""
    for text in ["hello", "test", "a"]:
        left, right = split_text(text, 0)
        assert left == "", f"Failed for text: {text}"
        assert right == text, f"Failed for text: {text}"


def test_split_progression():
    """Test that splitting at sequential positions works correctly."""
    text = "hello"
    
    for pos in range(len(text) + 1):
        left, right = split_text(text, pos)
        assert left + right == text or left.replace(" ", "") + right.replace(" ", "") == text
        assert len(left) <= pos or all(c == ' ' for c in left[pos:])
